plan.name: Split exhausted conformance batches before escalating memory
plan.summary: Complete step 3 of parent #549 in one plumbing change: after confirmed Java memory exhaustion and joined cleanup, release a divisible conformance batch's ordinary slot and lazily regenerate two nonempty contiguous halves from the existing disk store, recursively covering starting states, sorted steps, each declared attempt independently and tried states with correct local indexes and original diagnostics. Use an explicit optional runner capability carrying logical ranges, recovery completion and a typed exhaustion result, preserving the existing Check interface and generic TLC classification and retry policy; bounded demand-driven scheduling must use ordinary FIFO admission, preserve earliest logical failure, join canceled work, share the original deadline and admitted execution allowance throughout a recovery tree, and allow only singleton conformance obligations one existing exclusive retry without resetting the one-stall-retry limit, headroom, rounding or cleanup rules. Make the existing-Python wrapper understand logical completion rather than directory suffixes or failed intermediate calls, retain its deterministic failure prefix and authenticated invocation provenance, retain actual completed leaf checks in checks and add logical_checks records with module, batch, input_sha256, config and aggregate outcome (plus applicable failure evidence), without invented TLC counts or successful parent evidence, and keep successful ordinary and explicit/legacy Python fingerprints independent of splitting while still binding logical inputs, configurations, verdicts and counterexamples. Extend tlc_attempts with optional parent_check, parent_attempt, range {kind,start,count} using zero-based half-open logical ranges of init/steps/strict/tried units, and split=true on the exhausted attempt replaced by children, retaining unique portable check identities, all allocations and diagnostics, detached snapshots, old-report readability and JSON round trips; show these relationships and reasons in feedback and Markdown receipts, and intentionally replace only the conformance escalation expectations and size-insensitive fakes in large_tlc_540_accept_test.go and tlc_python_history_regression_test.go while preserving their ordinary model escalation assertions and all semantic, concurrent, strict-refusal and deterministic-prefix tests. Update SPEC.md and docs/gate.md for halving, concurrent ordinary allocations, singleton escalation, evidence/history separation and bounded memory/disk ownership, citing #578's ratified plan and recorded foundations D-0029, D-0047, D-0085, D-0090, D-0111, D-0185, D-0199, D-0306, D-0315, D-0322, D-0325 and D-0329 plus #392 and #569; run affected Go suites including shuffled repeated race coverage, let PR CI run affected real Python/TLAPS opt-ins, and leave decision recording for the new split policy refining D-0322 and any other unavailable Docker/network integration checks as Merger work without writing decisions/.

tests.name: TestConformance578OrdinaryHalves
tests.says: Real tlc.Runner calls through fake Docker recursively halve odd-sized Init, Next, strict accepted/refused and tried windows at unchanged ordinary memory limits alongside unrelated work, regenerate only local states, cover each leaf unit exactly once and match an unsplit semantic reference, including standalone and unknown-capacity runners.

tests.name: TestConformance578OriginalDiagnostics
tests.says: A failure in a right-hand descendant maps to the original endpoints, exact declared action/arguments/outcome, bad start or untried state; exhausted partial output supplies no counterexample or success.

tests.name: TestConformance578EarliestFailureAndBoundedScheduling
tests.says: An earlier recovering batch survives a later completed failure, returns the earliest logical failure and admits children through ordinary shared capacity without holding parent slots or exceeding the established concurrency bound.

tests.name: TestConformance578ClassificationAndSingletons
tests.says: Only classified exhaustion splits, including TLC memory frames and wrapped causes; ordinary errors, trace text and exit 137 do not, and only singleton obligations get one unchanged exclusive retry after ordinary work drains, with persistent exhaustion, missing headroom and unknown capacity bounded.

tests.name: TestConformance578RecoveryCleanupAndCancellation
tests.says: OOM cleanup precedes child admission, cancellation and original deadlines stop and join a split tree without further children or escalation, stores and modules are removed, and stalls retain one identical retry without renewal on singleton escalation.

tests.name: TestGate578SplitHistoryAndFingerprint
tests.says: An ordinary gate records the complete parent/child range tree and allocations with portable distinct identities in JSON, feedback and receipts, preserves detached snapshots and old reports, and has the same successful evidence fingerprint as its unsplit reference.

tests.name: TestPythonGate578SplitEvidence
tests.says: Explicit and legacy existing-Python gates recover divisible OOMs without deadlock or OperationalError, retain completed-child evidence separately from logical obligations and authenticated provenance/counts, preserve successful fingerprints across split schedules and JSON round trips, and retain generic model escalation.
